newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil delays civil service reform voting, again.
newsitem.headline: Brazil delays civil service reform voting, again.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies has delayed by yet another week voting on outstanding amendments to the government's civil service reform bil, a government spokeswoman in Congress said.

Wednesday in the lower house of Congress was taken up with voting on amendments to a telecommunications bill, said a spokeswoman for the government's leader in the lower house Deputy Luis Eduardo Magalhaes.
"The telecommunications bill is important as well so the civil service reform will have to wait," she said.

Government whips earlier said they would seek to revive the floundering civil service reform bill by holding votes on the remaining amendments. The bill itself was approved in April but since then the government has blocked votes on key amendments amid concerns it could not muster the three-fifths majorities needed to kill the proposed changes.
One amendment would make a mockery of the reform by allowing public sector workers to keep lifetime job guarantees.
The spokeswoman said voting on the amendments might resume next week, the last before a scheduled month-long recess in Congress during the month of July.
